1) Routed billing via Azure (they want single invoice) — Azure will support with push-through billing but we need to confirm pass-through of taxes/fees.
2) 20% upfront credit — ok but prefer it applied as monthly amortized credits vs. lump sum to preserve cashflow.

4) Termination for convenience / audit clauses — Finovate legal often pushes for 30-day TFC; we prefer 90/limited to trial usage.

Laura / team — here's my recommended approach after quick review:
- Billing: Accept routed billing. Add language that Azure will be the billing intermediary and that Redwood's invoices will be for reconciliation only; taxes/fees are passed by Azure per their billing policy.
- 20% credit: counter with amortized credit across first 6 invoices and a minimum committed ARR threshold ($150k) to avoid small-deal inefficiency.
- Termination: Keep 90-day TFC for commercial contracts; offer 30-day TFC limited to cause-free small pilot (<$25k actual spend) and require 30 days' notice with pro-rata charges.
- Indemnity / liability cap: propose standard Redwood cap (2x ARR or $5M whichever is lower).
- Data residency & compliance: provide SOC 2 Type II report and security pack; add audit bandwidth clause limited to one audit per 12 months.

I'll draft the term sheet and a marked MSA redline. Marcus — can you confirm if co-sell support (listing + 1-hour enablement + pipeline registration) is doable from GTM?

-Neha
